names: UCSF Mission Bay Housing North Building
summary: A 7-10 story mid-rise student and postdoctoral-scholar housing building at 525 Nelson Rising Lane (OpenStreetMap), one of four buildings in UCSF's Mission Bay Block 20 housing complex (with Hearst Tower and the West and South buildings, per UCSF's housing page). The November 2002 UC Regents item anticipated full occupancy of the complex by October 2005; no source read states when it actually opened.

milestones.text: UC Regents' Grounds and Buildings and Finance committees approve, and vote to present to the Board, a $112,816,000 budget and external financing for the Mission Bay Block 20 Housing and Retail Project -- one 15-story tower and three mid-rise buildings around a shared courtyard, 298,800 residential asf and 430 apartment units total -- with construction to begin June 2003 and full occupancy anticipated by October 2005

SFGate reports that, with the Helen Diller building's opening, the Mission Bay campus 'now has four research buildings, a community center and four residential buildings', so the Block 20 housing complex this building belongs to was complete by May 2009; no source read gives the date it actually opened (the November 2002 Regents item had anticipated full occupancy by October 2005)

facts.value: Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM) with Fisher Friedman Associates

open_questions: Could not confirm whether all four housing buildings opened in exactly the same month, or whether some phased in slightly later than others.
No exact unit count found for this specific building (only the four-building complex total).
No openly licensed image was found; none is hosted here.

Images: no plan drawing, elevation or openly-licensed photograph was found for this building specifically. Searched: UCSF Real Estate's Mission Bay campus-site and LRDP pages (realestate.ucsf.edu, which could not be checked); the UCSF 2014 LRDP EIR's CEQAnet filing (SCH 2013092047, whose pre-2016 attachments aren't hosted on CEQAnet itself); a May 2000 Regents Committee on Grounds and Buildings design-approval item for an early Mission Bay building (text-only, no figures); the 2008 "UCSF Mission Bay Planning Principles" appendix (a citywide-scale community map, no individual buildings labeled); and a UCSF wayfinding campus map (not an adopted plan, EIR or permit filing, so not eligible as public-record even though found). Not pursued further; the record's own project sources above remain the citation for the building's history. The same September 2008 Regents presentation (used for Byers Hall, Genentech Hall, Rock Hall and Rutter Center) includes one more photo on its "Architectural Context" slide labeled only "Housing," showing what looks like more than one building together; it wasn't used here because it can't be confidently attributed to this specific one.

The November 2002 Regents item covers the whole Block 20 project (one tower plus three mid-rise buildings) rather than naming this building individually; identification of this record as one of the three mid-rise buildings follows from its own facts entry, not a direct name match in the Regents record.

Searched for a cost figure specific to this building alone (versus the whole four-building Block 20 project). The only figure found anywhere is the November 2002 Regents item's own $112,816,000 project budget, which the Regents item itself states as a whole-project total covering Hearst Tower and all three mid-rise buildings together -- no source breaks it down per building, so no record-scope figure is added here; a per-project figure belongs in a site- or phase-scope table, not this record's own costs.

As of 2026-09-29, no source read states when the building actually opened; the 2005 opening shown earlier rested only on a housing page that could not be checked and on Langan, which gives no date. The milestone now carries the October 2005 full occupancy anticipated by the November 2002 Regents item, marked expected. 'Student and faculty' was changed to 'student, postdoctoral scholar and family' housing because Langan and the Regents item say so and no readable source mentions faculty.

Corrected 2026-10-06 (accuracy audit, October 2026): the October 2005 'full occupancy anticipated' milestone was shown as an expected completion although its date passed two decades ago and no source confirms it. The completion milestone now rests on SFGate's May 31, 2009 report that the campus had four residential buildings, which bounds the opening but does not date it; the actual opening date is still unconfirmed (a July 2005 UCSF news item, 'Community Center, Housing Complex Nearly Complete', could not be read). The approval milestone no longer names individual buildings, because the Regents item names none.
